div.head: Wl art 9
div.ab: Ego prohibeo, ut nullus uendat hominem extra patriam super plenam forisfacturam meam.
Ego prohibeo ut nullus vendat hominem extra patriam super plenam forisfacturam meam.
I forbid anyone to sell a man out of the country, under pain of incurring the full fine for insubordination to me.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 242–243 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 488, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

C. 9 und 10 reformieren beide die Art der Kriminalstrafe und stehen auch nebeneinander in der Vorlage; s. o. Einl. 2. 5. Die erste Person Sing. beweist zwar an sich nicht Authentizität; allein auch der Inhalt entspricht dem wirklichen Rechte und der Idee der Zeit. Und das Verbot c. 9 nur des ausländischen Sklavenhandels lautet beschränkter, also wohl archaischer als die Synode von 1102; vgl. Gl unfrei 12g. h.

Capp. 9 and 10 both reform the kind of criminal punishment, and they also stand side by side in the source; see above Introduction 2. 5. The first person singular does not in itself prove authenticity; but the content too corresponds to the actual law and the ideas of the time. And the prohibition in c. 9, of the foreign slave trade only, is more restricted, and so probably more archaic, than that of the synod of 1102; cf. Gl unfrei 12g. h.
